items.title: Fact 12: deterministic normalized-mass bounds

source.anchor: §6.4 Fact 12, equation (60) and complete immediate proof

items.statement: For every pair of nonnegative real numbers g,b with strictly positive sum, b/(g+b) is bounded above by b+(1-sqrt(g))², which is bounded above by b+(1-g)².
assumptions: g+b is strictly positive; neither individual number must be strictly positive.

obligations.label: Bound the bad fraction by bad mass plus square-root error
Bound square-root error by quadratic error

bindings.boundary: Fact 12 only. Theorem 7's normalized random-mass substitution, all moment bounds and the three main query theorems remain open. No expected-ratio conclusion is supplied as a hypothesis.

assumption_deltas.lean: g b : ℝ; hg : 0≤g; hb : 0≤b; hpos : 0<g+b
assumption_deltas.reason: Every scalar condition is explicit. Zero individual masses are retained. The source's hb is algebraically redundant but preserved, not added as an API restriction.

assumption_deltas.source: Nonnegative square root and ordinary division by positive total mass
assumption_deltas.lean: Real.sqrt g and totalized real division, with hg and hpos
assumption_deltas.reason: The hypotheses put both operations on their ordinary source domain. No measurability or integrability hypotheses belong to this pointwise real fact; those must be proved at its probabilistic consumer.
